The one non-statutory element, the effect of the life interest reserved to the donor in Deed of Gift No.1100, is supplied by the terms of the instrument as recited in the background rather than by any rule of law that has to be proved: the deed is stated to be an absolute and irrevocable gift subject to the donor's life interest, and the donor died. Jayaweera Licensed Surveyor in extent 20 perches was allotted to Sujeewa Jayamini. She was married to Thilak Gamage and had 2 children namely Dinesh and Iresh. By Deed of Gift No.1100 dated 12th January 2006 attested by Asanka Silva Notary Public, the said Lot A was gifted to her son Dinesh Gamage as an absolute and irrevocable gift subject to life interest of the said Donor Sujeewa Jayamini. gold_answer_draft.issue: The question is how title to Lot A, allotted to Sujeewa Jayamini by the final decree of 20 October 2001, passed by Deed of Gift No.1100 and then through three successive intestacies (Dinesh Gamage in 2009, Neesha Gamage in 2012 and Kasun Gamage in 2015) to the persons who now own the land and house, and how that chain is set out as a pedigree. A subsidiary issue is whether the general law of intestate succession applies to this family.
gold_answer_draft.rule: Inheritance ab intestato to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by Part III of the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance No. 15 of 1876 (s.21), "immovable property" including land and things attached to the earth (s.3), and Part III applying to the estate of anyone dying after the proclamation of the Ordinance (s.20). The Ordinance does not apply to Kandyans, Muslims or Tamils of the Northern Province subject to the Thesawalamai (s.2); nothing in the facts brings any of these persons within those systems, and the analysis proceeds on the general law. A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the estate of the intestate (s.22), and the remaining half devolves in the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals (s.23). Children and remoter descendants are preferent to all others, all children taking equally per capita and the issue of a predeceased child taking per stirpes by representation (s.24). Where descendants fail and only one parent is alive, the surviving parent takes half and the full brothers and sisters, together with the half-brothers and sisters related through the deceased parent and the issue of any of them by representation, take the other half (s.25). Where descendants fail and both parents have failed, the estate goes to the brothers and sisters, whether of the whole or half blood, and their issue by representation (s.26); and where all the half-brothers and sisters are related to the intestate on one side only, they take the whole, unless a grandparent or higher ascendant on the other side is alive (s.29). Persons equally near in degree take per capita and not per stirpes (s.30). A deed transferring an interest in immovable property must be notarially executed to avail in law (Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2).
gold_answer_draft.application: Sujeewa Jayamini became sole owner of Lot A under the final decree of 20 October 2001. By Deed of Gift No.1100 of 12 January 2006, notarially attested as the Prevention of Frauds Ordinance s.2 requires, she gifted Lot A to her son Dinesh Gamage absolutely and irrevocably, reserving a life interest to herself; the gift therefore vested ownership in Dinesh at once, burdened only by that life interest, and her husband Thilak Gamage and her other son Iresh took no interest in Lot A. On her death on 21 April 2007 the reserved life interest came to an end and Dinesh held the entirety free of it. Dinesh died intestate on 23 November 2009 owning the whole of Lot A, which is immovable property within Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance s.3, so ss.21 to 30 govern. His widow Lochana took one-half under s.22. Under s.23 and s.24 the other half went to his descendants, who at that date were four children, Neesha (his daughter by his first wife Nimali), Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi; being equally near in degree they took per capita under s.30, that is one-quarter of the half, or one-eighth of the land, each. Neesha died intestate on 20 May 2012 leaving her husband Rohan Jayaweera but no children. Under s.22 Rohan took one-half of her one-eighth. Her descendants having failed and both her parents having predeceased her (Dinesh on 23 November 2009 and Nimali on 15 July 2010), the other half of her share passed under s.26 to her brothers and sisters. Her only collaterals were Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi, half-siblings related to her on her father's side alone, so under s.29 they took the whole of that collateral half, per capita under s.30, no grandparent or higher ascendant on the mother's side being disclosed by the facts. Kasun Gamage died on 5 July 2015 unmarried and issueless, holding his original one-eighth together with the share he had taken from Neesha. He left neither spouse nor descendants; his father Dinesh had predeceased him and his mother Lochana survived him. Under s.25 Lochana as the surviving parent took half of his share, and the other half went to his full brother Kavindu and his full sister Piyumi, equally under s.30. Neesha, who would otherwise have been a half-sister on the father's side, had already died in 2012 without issue, so no share fell to her or to anyone representing her.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The pedigree runs: Sujeewa Jayamini (owner under the final decree of 20 October 2001, married to Thilak Gamage, children Dinesh and Iresh) gifted Lot A by Deed of Gift No.1100 of 12 January 2006 to Dinesh Gamage subject to her life interest, which determined on her death on 21 April 2007, leaving Dinesh sole owner. Dinesh died intestate on 23 November 2009, and Lot A devolved on his widow Lochana and his four children Neesha, Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi. Neesha died intestate on 20 May 2012 without children, and her interest devolved on her husband Rohan Jayaweera and on her half-siblings Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi. Kasun died intestate on 5 July 2015 unmarried and issueless, and his interest devolved on his mother Lochana and his full siblings Kavindu and Piyumi. The present owners are therefore Lochana Gamage, Kavindu Gamage, Piyumi Gamage and Rohan Jayaweera. This devolution assumes that the general law of the Ordinance, and not Kandyan law, Muslim law or the Thesawalamai, governs the family, and that no maternal grandparent of Neesha survived her for the purposes of the proviso to s.29.

answer_claims.claim_text: Inheritance ab intestato to immovable property in Sri Lanka is governed by the Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance, whatever the deceased person's domicile, and land with a house on it is immovable property for that purpose.

Part III of the Ordinance applies to the estate of any person dying after the proclamation of the Ordinance, but the Ordinance does not apply to Kandyans, Muslims or Tamils of the Northern Province subject to the Thesawalamai.
A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the intestate's property, and the remaining half devolves in the order descendants, ascendants, collaterals.
Children are preferent to all others in the estate of a parent and take equally per capita, the issue of a predeceased child taking by representation; persons equally near in degree take per capita.

Where descendants fail and both parents have failed, the estate goes to the brothers and sisters of the whole or half blood and their issue by representation, and where all the half-siblings are related on one side only they take the whole, subject to a surviving ascendant on the other side.

Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, the surviving parent takes half and the full brothers and sisters, with the half-siblings related through the deceased parent and their issue by representation, take the other half.

Deed of Gift No.1100 of 12 January 2006, being a notarially attested deed, vested ownership of Lot A in Dinesh Gamage subject to the life interest reserved to Sujeewa Jayamini, and that life interest determined on her death on 21 April 2007, leaving Dinesh sole owner.

On the intestacy of Dinesh Gamage on 23 November 2009, Lot A devolved on his widow Lochana as to one-half and on his four children Neesha, Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi as to the other half in equal per capita shares, his brother Iresh taking nothing.

On the intestacy of Neesha Gamage on 20 May 2012, her husband Rohan Jayaweera took one-half of her share, and because she left no descendants and both her parents had predeceased her, the other half passed to her half-siblings Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi, who as half-siblings on the father's side alone took the whole of that portion in equal shares.

On the intestacy of Kasun Gamage on 5 July 2015, he leaving no spouse and no issue, his surviving mother Lochana took half of his accumulated share and his full siblings Kavindu and Piyumi took the other half in equal shares, Neesha having already died without issue in 2012.
The present owners of the land and house are Lochana Gamage, Kavindu Gamage, Piyumi Gamage and Rohan Jayaweera.
The pedigree is stated on the assumption that the general law and not Kandyan law, Muslim law or the Thesawalamai governs this family, and that no maternal grandparent of Neesha survived her.

No judicial authority or non-statutory doctrine is needed once the deed of gift is taken at its recited terms.

gold_answer_draft.issue: The question is what undivided fraction of Lot A, the land and premises at Assessment No.12, Rajamalwatta Road, Panagoda, in extent 20 perches, each surviving heir presently owns after the three intestacies of Dinesh Gamage, Neesha Gamage and Kasun Gamage.
gold_answer_draft.rule: A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the intestate's property (Matrimonial Rights and Inheritance Ordinance s.22) and, subject to that half, the estate devolves first on descendants (s.23). Children take equally per capita (s.24), and persons equally near in degree take per capita and not per stirpes (s.30). Where descendants fail and both parents have failed, the estate goes to brothers and sisters of the whole or half blood and their issue by representation (s.26); where all the half-siblings are related to the intestate on one side only they take the whole, unless an ascendant on the other side survives (s.29). Where descendants fail and only one parent survives, that parent takes half and the full brothers and sisters, together with the half-siblings related through the deceased parent and their issue by representation, take the other half (s.25). The Ordinance governs intestate succession to immovable property in Sri Lanka (s.21, s.3) and does not apply to Kandyans, Muslims or Tamils of the Northern Province subject to the Thesawalamai (s.2).
gold_answer_draft.application: Dinesh Gamage owned the whole of Lot A when he died intestate on 23 November 2009. His widow Lochana took one-half under s.22. The other half went under ss.23, 24 and 30 to his four children then living, Neesha, Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi, that is one-eighth of the land each. On Neesha's intestacy on 20 May 2012 her one-eighth split under s.22 as to one-half, namely one-sixteenth of the land, to her husband Rohan Jayaweera; the balance one-sixteenth passed under s.26 to her collaterals, who were only her paternal half-siblings, so under s.29 they took that whole one-sixteenth and under s.30 divided it equally, one forty-eighth each to Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi. Each of the three then held one-eighth plus one forty-eighth, that is seven forty-eighths. Kasun died on 5 July 2015 unmarried and issueless holding seven forty-eighths. His father having predeceased him and his mother surviving, s.25 gave Lochana half of seven forty-eighths, namely seven ninety-sixths, and gave his full siblings Kavindu and Piyumi the other half in equal shares, namely seven one hundred and ninety-seconds each. Lochana therefore holds one-half plus seven ninety-sixths. Kavindu and Piyumi each hold seven forty-eighths plus seven one hundred and ninety-seconds. Rohan Jayaweera holds the one-sixteenth he took in 2012. Expressed over a common denominator of 192, Lochana holds 110/192, Kavindu 35/192, Piyumi 35/192 and Rohan 12/192, which together account for the whole.
gold_answer_draft.conclusion: The present shares in Lot A are: Lochana Gamage 55/96 (110/192); Kavindu Gamage 35/192; Piyumi Gamage 35/192; and Rohan Jayaweera 1/16 (12/192). These fractions total unity. They assume that the general law applies to this family rather than Kandyan law, Muslim law or the Thesawalamai, and that no maternal grandparent or higher maternal ascendant of Neesha Gamage was alive on 20 May 2012, since the proviso to s.29 would otherwise halve the portion taken by her paternal half-siblings.

answer_claims.claim_text: A surviving spouse inherits one-half of the intestate's property and the remaining half devolves first on descendants, who take equally per capita when equally near in degree.

Where an intestate leaves no descendants and both parents have failed, the collateral portion goes to brothers and sisters of the whole or half blood, and half-siblings related on one side only take the whole of it subject to a surviving ascendant on the other side.
Where an intestate leaves no descendants and one parent survives, that parent takes half and the full brothers and sisters take the other half.
On the intestacy of Dinesh Gamage in 2009 Lochana took 1/2 of Lot A and Neesha, Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi took 1/8 each.

On the intestacy of Neesha Gamage in 2012 her husband Rohan Jayaweera took 1/16 of Lot A and her paternal half-siblings Kasun, Kavindu and Piyumi took 1/48 each, so that each of the three then held 7/48.
On the intestacy of Kasun Gamage in 2015 his mother Lochana took 7/96 of Lot A and his full siblings Kavindu and Piyumi took 7/192 each.
Lochana Gamage presently owns 55/96, that is 110/192, of Lot A.
Kavindu Gamage and Piyumi Gamage each presently own 35/192 of Lot A.
Rohan Jayaweera presently owns 1/16, that is 12/192, of Lot A.
The four shares of 110/192, 35/192, 35/192 and 12/192 exhaust the whole of Lot A, and they assume that the general law applies and that no maternal ascendant of Neesha Gamage survived her.
